beatOutlines.textOutline: It is 10 AM, and Raju stares at the screen with intense excitement.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji immediately puts down his tea cup and cautions Raju.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju ignores the advice and executes the trade at ₹580.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju entered at ₹580, right at the peak of Wave 5.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Within hours, three corrective waves slammed the stock down to ₹510.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The market advances in five impulse waves and breathes through three corrective waves.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The first pillar is the basic 5-3 cycle and its connection to Dow Theory.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The second pillar is corrective patterns: the internal structure of zigzags, flats, and triangles.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The third pillar is the rule of alternation, channeling techniques, and Wave 4 support.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: According to R.N. Elliott, the market progresses in five waves in trend direction: 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: This is followed by three corrective waves labeled A, B, and C against the trend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remember the cardinal rule: Wave 4 can never overlap into the price territory of Wave 1.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Dow Theory divided a bull market into three phases: accumulation, public participation, and distribution.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Elliott Wave moulds this exact Dow structure into a precise mathematical formula of five waves.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Dow Theory identifies trend direction, while Elliott Wave projects specific turning points and price levels.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Corrective Wave Types: Zigzag vs Flat
scenes.concept: Corrective Wave Types: Zigzag vs Flat

beatOutlines.textOutline: A zigzag correction is a sharp and deep 5-3-5 sub-wave structure.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A flat correction is a sideways 3-3-5 structure where Wave B tests the top of Wave A.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remember: in a zigzag Wave A is 5 waves, whereas in a flat Wave A is merely 3 waves.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

takeaways: Corrective Wave Types: Zigzag vs Flat

beatOutlines.textOutline: In triangles, volatility continuously contracts between buyers and sellers.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In Elliott Wave, triangles appear almost exclusively in Wave 4, never in Wave 2.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The moment sub-wave 'e' completes, the market launches into a powerful final Wave 5 thrust.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The rule of alternation states that the market rarely behaves the same way twice in a row.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If Wave 2 was a sharp zigzag correction causing a deep retracement...
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: ...then Wave 4 will almost certainly be a sideways flat or a time-consuming triangle.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: To construct an Elliott channel, first connect the peaks of Wave 1 and Wave 3 with a trendline.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Then a parallel line projected across bottoms of Waves 2 and 4 yields the exact selling target for Wave 5.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And when the major correction follows 5 waves, the bottom of Wave 4 serves as the strongest support zone.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now it's your turn. Examine the question appearing on the screen carefully.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think. Recall the Rule of Alternation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The correct answer: a sideways Flat or horizontal Triangle that consumes time rather than price depth.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Before market close, Raju approaches Sharma ji with his notebook.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji smiles and explains the real lesson of professional trading to Raju.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju realizes that one buys on logic at Wave 4 support, not in FOMO at the peak.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The entire Elliott Wave Principle is woven through eight foundational links.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Five waves in trend direction and three waves counter-trend complete the full cycle.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The three phases of Dow Theory align cleanly with Elliott's first, third, and fifth waves.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Zigzags plunge deep with 5-3-5, while flats consolidate sideways with 3-3-5.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The rule of alternation and prior Wave 4 support establish high-probability trading setups.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Today's lesson: Trend in 5, correct in 3—master the wave count and control your emotions.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Five impulse waves (1-2-3-4-5) drive the primary trend
Three corrective waves (A-B-C) balance the cycle
Dow accumulation, participation, distribution match waves 1, 3, 5
Cardinal rule: Wave 4 never violates Wave 1 territory
Zigzag is a sharp 5-3-5, while Flat is a sideways 3-3-5
Triangles form contracting 3-3-3-3-3 coils in Wave 4
Rule of Alternation mandates sharp vs sideways contrast
Prior Wave 4 bottom acts as prime support for entire corrections
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
